_comment: RESEARCHER output (Phase 1). Facts gathered 2026-09-29 from public GitHub pages and vendor pricing pages. Scores are 1-10. Edit scores here, then re-run scripts/decide.py; the STRATEGIST decision is recomputed from this file.

ccxt.facts: 44.2k stars, 8.9k forks, 241 open issues, MIT, ~101k commits, 100+ exchanges, Python/JS/Go/C#/PHP/Java/Rust

reasons.trading: De-facto standard unified exchange API; free historical OHLCV from exchanges (Binance spot has years of 1h/1d candles). freqtrade uses it internally.
reasons.investing: Crypto only; useful for long-term crypto holdings data but no equities, no fundamentals.

ccxt.limitations: Library, not an app; history depth and rate limits depend on each exchange; exchange-specific quirks.

freqtrade.facts: 54.9k stars, 11.4k forks, 22 open issues, GPL-3.0, monthly releases (2026.6, 2026.7, 2026.8 on 2026-08-31), Python 3.11+, Docker images, Telegram + Web UI

reasons.trading: Most mature open-source crypto bot: dry-run (paper) mode built in, backtesting with fees, hyperopt, and built-in lookahead-analysis and recursive-analysis commands that directly detect look-ahead bias. Config-driven.
reasons.investing: Can hold positions long but has no portfolio-weight allocation or rebalancing model; crypto only.

freqtrade.limitations: Strategies are Python classes; backtests use candle data (no order book), so fills are approximate; hyperopt makes curve fitting easy.

jesse.facts: 8.6k stars, 1.3k forks, 7 open issues, MIT, no GitHub releases (ships via PyPI), docs.jesse.trade

reasons.trading: Clean backtester with Monte Carlo and rule-significance testing; good independent cross-check for freqtrade on the same candles.
reasons.investing: Crypto only; no equities, no allocation model. Cannot cross-check a stock portfolio.

jesse.limitations: Paper/live trading needs the live-trade plugin (license key; premium tier historically ~$1,600, a limited free tier exists). Backtesting itself is free. Smaller community.

nautilus_trader.facts: 29.5k stars, 3.9k forks, 131 open issues, LGPL-3.0, Rust core + Python, bi-weekly releases, 24+ adapters (Binance, Bybit, OKX, Interactive Brokers, Databento, Tardis)

reasons.trading: Highest-fidelity engine in the list: event-driven, nanosecond resolution, order-book/tick data; same code runs backtest and live. Ideal final validation.
reasons.investing: Supports equities via Interactive Brokers, but good equity data is paid (Databento) and it has no portfolio-optimisation layer.

nautilus_trader.limitations: Steep learning curve; breaking changes between releases (v2 release candidates not recommended for real capital); highest value needs tick/order-book data which is large or paid.

hummingbot.facts: 20.3k stars, 5.0k forks, 72 open issues, Apache-2.0, 50+ connectors (CEX + DEX), paper-trade connectors

reasons.trading: Specialist for market making / arbitrage with a real paper-trade mode, but MM edge depends on fee tier, latency and inventory risk that a retail user rarely controls.

hummingbot.limitations: Backtesting of MM is weak (queue position and adverse selection are not modelled on candles); paper MM results are systematically optimistic.

finrl.facts: 16.4k stars, 3.5k forks, 283 open issues, MIT, active commits (several on 2026-09-24..28), SB3 agents (A2C, PPO, SAC, TD3, DDPG), yfinance/Alpaca/FMP/ccxt processors

reasons.trading: RL on crypto candles is possible but results are highly seed- and period-dependent; weak baseline evidence.
reasons.investing: Has a portfolio-allocation environment that fits monthly rebalancing research; that is its strongest use.

finrl.limitations: Self-described educational/research framework; maintainers point production users to FinRL-X/FinRL-Trading. High open-issue count, dependency churn (PyTorch, SB3, pandas). RL overfits easily; needs many seeds and strict walk-forward.

ai_hedge_fund.facts: 63.8k stars, 11.2k forks, 54 open issues, MIT, ~930 commits, LLM investor-persona agents, needs financialdatasets.ai (no free tier: $20 for 1,000 requests or $200/month) plus an LLM API key

reasons.investing: Useful as a qualitative idea/analysis layer on a stock list, but not a validated signal.

ai_hedge_fund.limitations: Explicitly educational, not for real trading. Backtests are structurally contaminated: the LLM has read about the outcomes in its training data (look-ahead the project can only partially mask). Non-deterministic, paid per run, hard to walk-forward.

eliza.facts: 19.5k stars, 5.8k forks, 24 open issues, MIT, TypeScript on Node/Bun monorepo, Telegram/Discord connectors, EVM/Solana wallet features, no longer accepts third-party plugins

reasons.trading: Only relevant as the report/alert bot; neutral between paths.

eliza.limitations: Heavy framework for sending reports; ships wallet/on-chain actions that must be disabled so it can never trade. freqtrade's own Telegram bot already covers basic alerts.

finviz_elite.facts: Elite $39.50/month or $299.50/year; CSV/API export of screeners is Elite-only; free tier has no export; unofficial scrapers exist but automated access to the free site may breach their terms

reasons.trading: US equity snapshot screener; no crypto; not a short-term signal source.
reasons.investing: Excellent fundamentals/valuation filters for a US universe with a simple export.

finviz_elite.limitations: Snapshot of today only, no point-in-time history: back-testing today's screen over past years causes survivorship and look-ahead bias. Paid for export. No scraping without your explicit OK.

coinmarketcap_api.facts: Free Basic: 15,000 credits/month, 50 requests/minute, latest listings/quotes, only ~1 month of historical data; Builder $29/month adds 3 years of history

reasons.trading: Good for ranking, market cap, 24h volume and stablecoin tags to build a liquid universe.
reasons.investing: Crypto only; a long-term crypto allocation is possible but narrow.

coinmarketcap_api.limitations: Free plan cannot rebuild the historical top-50: using today's top-50 for a 3-year backtest is survivorship bias (dead coins are missing). Mitigate with fixed large caps (BTC/ETH) as primary evidence, or Builder plan for history.
